Check eligibility for housing assistance

  • See if you qualify

Energy efficiency assistance

  • Get help paying your energy bills

    The Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP) can help you pay for your energy bills. It also offers services to keep your power on and make your home use less energy.
    Learn more about home energy savings and services

  • Save money on your energy bills

    Get help making your home more energy efficient and lowering utility costs. Find out who qualifies and how to apply for money to fix your heating, cooling, and other home repairs.
    Start saving money on energy bills today

  • Free solar panels for eligible residents

    The MEA Solar Access Program helps Maryland residents who qualify get solar panels for free. These panels power homes with energy that is clean, costs less, and is good for the environment.
    Find out if you qualify for free solar panels

Tax credits

  • Homestead tax credit

    The Homestead Tax Credit keeps your property taxes from going up too much each year. It limits the increase in your home's taxable value to 10% or less, so you don't pay tax on the extra growth.
    Learn how to apply for the homestead tax credit

  • Property tax credit for low-income homeowners

    The Homeowners Property Tax Credit Program puts a limit on how much you pay in property taxes. The amount is based on how much money your family makes.
    Find out if you qualify based on the property tax requirements

Housing and rent assistance

  • Emergency assistance for families with children

    Get cash when you need it from the Emergency Assistance for Families with Children (EAFC) program. You can use it to pay rent or utilities, or for other family emergencies.
    Apply for Emergency Assistance for Families with Children

  • Rental subsidies for low-income residents

    Apply for or learn more about Maryland’s Housing Choice Voucher Program. Find contact information for each county. You can also see the waitlist status and links to details about state programs.
    Contact your local housing agency to apply for a rental voucher

  • Resources for renters

    Find housing, solve rent challenges, and apply for support. Connect to resources to prevent eviction and to seek legal help.
    Explore support for renters

  • Know your rights

    Learn more about your rights as a renter. This includes protections under federal and state laws, like the Maryland Renters’ Rights and Stabilization Act.
    Learn about your rights as a renter

  • Independent living support for older adults

    The Supporting Older Adults with Resources (SOAR) program helps older adults access services that support independence. These include case management, home-based support, and partial financial assistance for assisted living.

Individual Taxes

See how Maryland is making it simple, safe, and efficient to file your taxes.

Skip sidebar navigation

Tax filing

  • Pay your taxes

    Read how to complete your tax payment using a method that works for you. You can also learn about estimated payments and withholding.
    Learn how to pay your individual taxes

  • File your taxes

    Get the resources to file with confidence. Find tax calculators, forms, as well as information on tax credits and refunds.
    Learn more about how to file individual taxes

  • File for an extension

    If you need more time to file your taxes, find out how to get an extension.
    Read how to file for an tax extension

  • Tax calculators

    See how much you should pay for taxes. Use these calculators to estimate how much to pay and how much to withhold.
    Get tax estimates

  • Request tax filing help

    Get answers to your tax filing questions. You can use the online portal or make an appointment.
    Learn more about tax services

  • Find unclaimed property

    Check this free service to see if you have any unclaimed property or money. Follow the steps to claim what's rightfully yours.
    See if there is unclaimed property owed to you

  • Where's my refund?

    Use this system to track the status of your current year Maryland income tax refund.
    Check the status of your tax refund

Tax credits

  • Individual taxpayer credits

    Browse a list of commonly used tax credits, and see if you’re eligible to claim any of them.
    Explore individual taxpayer credits

  • Homestead tax credit

    The Homestead Tax Credit keeps your property taxes from going up too much each year. It limits the increase in your home's taxable value to 10% or less, so you don't pay tax on the extra growth.
    Learn how to apply for the homestead tax credit

  • Property tax credit for low-income homeowners

    The Homeowners Property Tax Credit Program puts a limit on how much you pay in property taxes. The amount is based on how much money your family makes.
    Find out if you qualify based on the property tax requirements

  • Renter's tax credits

    If your rent is high compared to your income, you may qualify for a tax credit of up to $1,000.
    See if you qualify for this tax credit

Maryland.gov Acceptable Use & Linking Policy

General Policy

Maryland.gov is the official web portal for the Maryland State government and is maintained by the Maryland Department of Information Technology (DoIT). Individual state agency websites are separately maintained by the respective agency.

Links to Government Websites

Maryland.gov links to publicly available websites that are government-owned or government-sponsored websites in domains such as .gov, .us, .mil, and .fed. Maryland.gov may link to: quasi-government agencies and websites created by public sector/private sector partnerships and some government-sponsored websites that end in .com, .org, or .net.

Links to Non-Government Websites

DoIT may, at its discretion, provide links to websites of nonprofit organizations and private or commercial entities if they offer information or services related to topics covered on the Maryland.gov website and are consistent with the purpose of the Maryland.gov website. All requests for links to non-governmental sites will be evaluated on a case-by-case basis. DoIT neither endorses nor guarantees in any way the external organizations, services, advice, or products included in these website links. Furthermore, DoIT neither controls nor guarantees the accuracy, relevance, timeliness, or completeness of the information contained in non-government website links.

Link Evaluation Criteria

DoIT evaluates all links using the following criteria:

  • Is the website an official government-owned or supported website?
  • Does the website provide government information and/or services in a way that is not available on an official government website?
  • Does the website complement existing information, products, and services on Maryland.gov?
  • Is the website accessible and applicable to a wide audience?
  • Is the website's content relevant, useful, and authoritative for citizens, businesses, and/or government officials?
  • Does the website's information appear to be accurate and current?
  • Is the website's approach to the privacy of personal information consistent with Maryland.gov’s privacy and security policies?
  • Is the primary intent of the website to educate and inform, rather than persuade, convert, or sell? The site may include advertising but must be free from heavy marketing or promotion of products.
  • Does the website provide information free of charge?

Linking to Maryland.gov

Linking to the Maryland.gov web portal or Maryland state agency websites is permitted with the following limitations:

  • You may not capture Maryland.gov pages within frames or present Maryland.gov content as your own.
  • You may not state or imply that the State of Maryland, DoIT, or Maryland.gov is endorsing your product, site, or services.

Maryland.gov does not engage in reciprocal linking.

Prohibitions

Maryland.gov will not link to any website that contains the following types of content:

  • Sites that exhibit hate, bias, discrimination, pornography, libelous or otherwise defamatory content;
  • Affiliation or advocacy of a political party, organization, or candidate running for office;
  • Content not suitable for readers or viewers of all ages;
  • Content that infringes on any trademark, copyright, or patent rights of another;
  • Content that a reasonable citizen may not consider maintaining the dignity and decorum appropriate for government.

Maryland.gov reserves the right to deny or remove any link that contains misleading information or unsubstantiated claims, or is determined to be in conflict with Maryland.gov’s mission or policies. ​

Check eligibility for health and medical benefits

  • See if you qualify

    Use our five-minute screener to find out what benefits you can get.
    Check your health and medical benefits eligibility now

  • Review and update your benefits information (redetermination)

    If you already have an account, sign in. You can see your information and renew your benefits.
    Log in to your existing benefits accounts to review or update your profile

General healthcare assistance

  • Maryland Health Connection

    Look at different health and dental insurance plans and pick the right one for you.
    Find out if you qualify and enroll in health and dental insurance plans

  • Free or low-cost health insurance

    Maryland has a Medicaid program. Learn about benefits for adults, kids, older adults, and people with disabilities.
    Explore your Medicaid options

  • Health coverage for uninsured children

    The Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP) gives free health coverage to kids. This is for families who do not make enough money to buy their own health insurance, but make too much money to get Medicaid.
    See if your family qualifies for the Maryland Children's Health Program

  • Get help paying for Medicare

    ​A Medicare Savings Program can help pay your Medicare Part A and Part B. If you qualify, the program might also pay for other medical expenses.
    Check if you’re eligible for Medicare support

  • Free medical equipment and assistive technology

    Maryland Equips provides free medical equipment and assistive technology. Anyone in Maryland who has an illness, injury, or disability can get this equipment for free.
    Find a pickup location near you

  • Support for older adults, people with disabilities, and caregivers

    Maryland Access Point (MAP) provides information and referrals on available financial, health, and support services for older adults, people with disabilities, and caregivers in Maryland.
    Explore MAP services and support

  • Healthy smiles

    The Maryland Healthy Smiles Dental Program (MHSDP) provides dental care to eligible Medicaid members. Medicaid covers a wide range of dental services.
    Learn more about the Maryland Healthy Smiles Dental Program

Specialized healthcare assistance

  • Free and low-cost screening for breast and cervical cancer

    The Breast and Cervical Cancer Program (BCCP) offers free or low-cost breast and cervical cancer tests.
    Find breast and cervical cancer screening services today

  • Free and low-cost breast and cervical cancer diagnosis and treatment

    The Breast and Cervical Cancer Diagnosis and Treatment (BCCDT) Program helps residents with breast or cervical cancer. Find free and low-cost treatment services.
    Learn about Breast and Cervical Cancer Diagnosis and Treatment (BCCDT)

  • Get help paying for HIV/AIDS medications

    Maryland AIDS Drug Assistance Program (MADAP) ensures that people have access to the medication they need to stay healthy.
    Enroll in the Maryland AIDS Drug Assistance Program (MADAP)

  • Medical cannabis

    Learn more about Maryland's medical cannabis program. Register, find a provider, and locate a dispensary near you.
    Learn how to legally obtain medical cannabis in Maryland

  • Mental health and substance use

    Services to help Marylanders with mental health, substance use disorders, and more.
    Find support for mental health and substance use

Health and medical

  • Health coverage for uninsured children

    The Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP) gives free health coverage to kids. This is for families who do not make enough money to buy their own health insurance, but make too much money to get Medicaid.
    See if your family qualifies for the Maryland Children's Health Program

  • Children with developmental disabilities

    The Maryland Developmental Disabilities Administration (DDA) offers many programs and services. They help disabled family members be part of the community, go to school, and find jobs.
    Get support for children with developmental disabilities

Support for children

  • Expecting and new parents

    Maryland offers a wide range of programs to support you during pregnancy and as your child grows.
    Find support for expecting and new parents

  • Child support

    Child support is money paid by one parent to the other, or to a legal guardian, to support a child. The Maryland Child Support Administration (CSA) works with both parents to help children grow and thrive.
    Explore child support resources

  • Adoption and guardianship

    Learn about adoption and being a guardian. You may be eligible to receive certain benefits to assist in supporting a child.
    Get more information on adoption

  • Out-of-home care (foster care)

    Read what it takes to become a resource parent, and make a positive difference in a child's life.
    Explore FAQs about out-of-home care

  • Child protective services

    These services are in place to make sure children do not live in unsafe places. They also support parents and caretakers in taking care of their kids.
    Learn about child protective services

  • Maryland Safe Haven

    A parent may not be ready to raise a child or start a family for various reasons. The Maryland Safe Haven Law allows them to surrender an infant without fear of arrest or prosecution.
    Learn more about the Safe Haven program

Financial assistance

  • Emergency assistance for families with children

    Get cash when you need it from the Emergency Assistance for Families with Children (EAFC) program. You can use it to pay rent or utilities, or for other family emergencies.
    Apply for Emergency Assistance for Families with Children

  • Temporary cash assistance

    The Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) program gives money to families with kids who need temporary help. It also helps them get ready to be independent through work.
    Learn how to apply for TCA

  • Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC)

    If you qualify, the EITC will either reduce or eliminate the amount of the state and local income tax that you owe.
    Check your eligibility for the EITC

  • Child care scholarship program

    The Child Care Scholarship Program helps families pay for child care and early education.
    See if you're eligible for child care support

  • Pre-K for low-income and homeless children

    Children whose families have low income or are experiencing homelessness can get free Prekindergarten. Pre-K offers children important skills to be ready for school.
    Find a Pre-K program near you

Food and nutrition

  • Food assistance for women and young children

    If you are pregnant, a new mother, or have a child under five, Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) can help. This program offers nutrition advice, breastfeeding support, and healthy foods.
    Learn about WIC and make an appointment today

  • Food assistance for low-income households

    The Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) helps low-income households buy healthy food.
    Find out how to apply for SNAP

  • SUN Bucks

    Eligible students (ages 5-18) can get money for food during the summer when school is out.
    Read more and get enrolled in SUN Bucks

Statewide Accessibility Policy

Global Accessibility Statement for State of Maryland Websites

Commitment to Accessibility

The State of Maryland is committed to ensuring digital accessibility for all individuals, including people with disabilities. We strive to make the content on our website accessible and usable for everyone, and to procure information technology that is accessible to all, in each case regardless of their abilities or disabilities. 

We are committed to meeting the requirements of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) Title II and Mary​land Non-Visual Access Clause and other relevant accessibility standards including the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG, 2.1 Level AA)​.

Reporting Accessibility Issues

If you encounter any accessibility barriers on our website, we encourage you to report them to us. Your feedback helps us improve the website and better serve all users. Please contact us by sending an email to: accessibility.doit@maryland.gov

Medical and financial assistance

  • Get help paying for Medicare

    Maryland has a Medicare Savings Program that can cover many out-of-pocket expenses if you qualify.
    Find out more about the Medicare Savings Program

  • Long term care services and supports

    Medicaid Long Term Care Services and Supports (LTSS) offers services with the goals of privacy, dignity, and respect. If eligible, people may receive long term care at home or in special facilities.
    Get long term care services that are right for you

  • Independent living support for older adults

    The Supporting Older Adults with Resources (SOAR) program helps older adults access services that support independence. These include case management, home-based support, and partial financial assistance for assisted living.
    Find out if you qualify for SOAR

Food and equipment

  • Food assistance for low-income households

    The Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) helps low-income households buy healthy food.
    Find out how to apply for SNAP

  • Farmers market money for older adults

    Eligible older adults can receive money to buy fresh fruits and vegetables. The money can be used at local farmers markets and farm stands.
    Apply to get your farmers market subsidy

  • Community meals for older adults

    There are more than 250 places in Maryland where older adults can get a meal. These spots are great for meeting people, learning about nutrition, and taking part in health programs.
    Find a community meal near you

  • Home delivered meals for older adults

    If you're an older adult with mobility issues, you might be eligible to get nutritious meals brought to you.
    Connect to a meal delivery service in your area

  • Free medical equipment and assistive technology

    Maryland Equips provides free medical equipment and assistive technology. Anyone in Maryland who has an illness, injury, or disability can get this equipment for free.
    Find a pickup location near you

Resources for older adults

  • Adult protective services

    This program is for adults aged 18 or older who cannot take care of themselves. It provides professional services to protect them from harm, abuse, or neglect.
    Learn about adult protective services

  • Support for older adults, people with disabilities, and caregivers

    Maryland Access Point (MAP) provides information and referrals on available financial, health, and support services for older adults, people with disabilities, and caregivers in Maryland.
    Explore MAP services and support

  • Get help navigating Medicare

    The Maryland State Health Insurance Assistance Program is here to help navigate issues related to Medicare.
    Learn more about Medicare support

  • Protect yourself

    Learn how to avoid Medicare fraud and abuse.
    Explore Medicare fraud resources

Financial Assistance

Explore programs to weather tough times and get back on track.

  • Find out if you qualify for financial assistance and apply
Skip sidebar navigation

Cash assistance

  • See if you qualify

    Use our five-minute screener to find out what benefits you can get.
    Check your eligibility for financial assistance

  • Temporary cash assistance

    The Temporary Cash Assistance (TCA) program gives money to families with kids who need temporary help. It also helps them get ready to be independent through work.
    Learn how to apply for TCA

  • Temporary assistance for people with disabilities

    If you have a disability and a low income, the Temporary Disability Assistance Program (TDAP) can help. It can take a while to get a decision about federal disability payments. This program gives you temporary cash while you wait.
    Read more about TDAP eligibility

  • Emergency assistance for families with children

    Get cash when you need it from the Emergency Assistance for Families with Children (EAFC) program. You can use it to pay rent or utilities, or for other family emergencies.
    Apply for Emergency Assistance for Families with Children

Health and medical

  • Maryland Health Connection

    Look at different health and dental insurance plans and pick the right one for you.
    Find out if you qualify and enroll in health and dental insurance plans

  • Free or low-cost health insurance

    Maryland has a Medicaid program. Learn about benefits for adults, kids, older adults, and people with disabilities.
    Explore your Medicaid options

  • Health coverage for uninsured children

    The Maryland Children's Health Program (MCHP) gives free health coverage to kids. This is for families who do not make enough money to buy their own health insurance, but make too much money to get Medicaid.
    See if your family qualifies for the Maryland Children's Health Program

  • Get help paying for Medicare

    ​A Medicare Savings Program can help pay your Medicare Part A and Part B. If you qualify, the program might also pay for other medical expenses.
    Check if you’re eligible for Medicare support

  • Financial assistance for employed people with disabilities

    The Employed Individuals with Disabilities (EID) Program helps you if you're working and have a disability. It lets you buy into Medicaid, even if you earn too much money to normally qualify.
    Learn if EID will work for you

  • Free medical equipment and assistive technology

    Maryland Equips provides free medical equipment and assistive technology. Anyone in Maryland who has an illness, injury, or disability can get this equipment for free.
    Find a pickup location near you

  • Free and low-cost screening for breast and cervical cancer

    The Breast and Cervical Cancer Program (BCCP) offers free or low-cost breast and cervical cancer tests.
    Find breast and cervical cancer screening services today

  • Free and low-cost breast and cervical cancer diagnosis and treatment

    The Breast and Cervical Cancer Diagnosis and Treatment (BCCDT) Program helps residents with breast or cervical cancer. Find free and low-cost treatment services.
    Learn about Breast and Cervical Cancer Diagnosis and Treatment (BCCDT)

  • Get help paying for HIV/AIDS medications

    Maryland AIDS Drug Assistance Program (MADAP) ensures that people have access to the medication they need to stay healthy.
    Enroll in the Maryland AIDS Drug Assistance Program (MADAP)

Housing

  • Get help paying your energy bills

    The Office of Home Energy Programs (OHEP) can help you pay for your energy bills. It also offers services to keep your power on and make your home use less energy.
    Learn more about home energy savings and services

  • Save money on your energy bills

    Get help making your home more energy efficient and lowering utility costs. Find out who qualifies and how to apply for money to fix your heating, cooling, and other home repairs.
    Start saving money on energy bills today

  • Free solar panels for eligible residents

    The MEA Solar Access Program helps Maryland residents who qualify get solar panels for free. These panels power homes with energy that is clean, costs less, and is good for the environment.
    Find out if you qualify for free solar panels

  • Rental subsidies for low-income residents

    Apply for or learn more about Maryland’s Housing Choice Voucher Program. Find contact information for each county. You can also see the waitlist status and links to details about state programs.
    Contact your local housing agency to apply for a rental voucher

  • Independent living support for older adults

    The Supporting Older Adults with Resources (SOAR) program helps older adults access services that support independence. These include case management, home-based support, and partial financial assistance for assisted living.
    Find out if you qualify for SOAR

Food and education

  • Food assistance for women and young children

    If you are pregnant, a new mother, or have a child under five, Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) can help. This program offers nutrition advice, breastfeeding support, and healthy foods.
    Learn about WIC and make an appointment today

  • Food assistance for low-income households

    The Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) helps low-income households buy healthy food.
    Find out how to apply for SNAP

  • Farmers market money for older adults

    Eligible older adults can receive money to buy fresh fruits and vegetables. The money can be used at local farmers markets and farm stands.
    Apply to get your farmers market subsidy

  • SUN Bucks

    Eligible students (ages 5-18) can get money for food during the summer when school is out.
    Read more and get enrolled in SUN Bucks

  • Child care scholarship program

    The Child Care Scholarship Program helps families pay for child care and early education.
    See if you're eligible for child care support

  • Scholarships for nonpublic schools

    The BOOST program provides scholarship awards for some low-income students to attend a participating nonpublic school.
    Find out if your child is eligible for a scholarship to a nonpublic school

Tax credits and debt relief

  • Homestead tax credit

    The Homestead Tax Credit keeps your property taxes from going up too much each year. It limits the increase in your home's taxable value to 10% or less, so you don't pay tax on the extra growth.
    Learn how to apply for the homestead tax credit

  • Property tax credit for low-income homeowners

    The Homeowners Property Tax Credit Program puts a limit on how much you pay in property taxes. The amount is based on how much money your family makes.
    Find out if you qualify based on the property tax requirements

  • Earned Income Tax Credit (EITC)

    If you qualify, the EITC will either reduce or eliminate the amount of the state and local income tax that you owe.
    Check your eligibility for the EITC

  • Get a tax credit for student loan payments

    Qualified applicants may use this tax credit to pay down their student loan debt.
    Find out if you qualify for tax credits on student loans

  • Loan repayment programs for employees in public service/healthcare fields

    There's help for those helping others in Maryland. Check out these programs for employees in public service, health care, and other fields.
    Learn more about loan repayment options and apply today

  • Resources for Maryland consumers

    Learn about mortgage relief and how to manage consumer debt.
    Explore ways to prevent debt

Other benefits

  • Burial assistance

    If your loved one was getting public assistance and you can't afford their funeral, this program can help.
    Get help with paying burial expenses

  • Transportation assistance

    Get a reliable used car and get on the road toward more job options and financial independence.
    See what's available through TAP

Driving and vehicle licenses

  • New drivers

    Read the manual and practice for your test. Learn the rules of the road and become a safe driver.
    Check out new driver resources

  • Renew your driver's license or ID

    See what you need to do to renew your driver's license, and get information for special cases. Renew online, by mail, or in person.
    Get your license or ID renewed

  • Renew your vehicle registration

    You can renew your vehicle registration online, by mail, or in person at offices near you.
    Explore your vehicle registration options

  • Driver's license for new residents

    If you're new, learn how to get a Maryland driver's license or identification card.
    Learn how new residents can get a Maryland driver's license

  • Titling your vehicle

    Learn what documents to gather and start the process to title your vehicle. You will need to make an in-person appointment to complete the process.
    Start your vehicle title pre-application

  • Commercial driver's license (CDL)

    Access quick information about applying for a permit or renewing your CDL.
    Find out more about CDLs

Certificates

  • Request a birth certificate

    Birth certificates may be requested in person by appointment, or ordered by mail. Read who may apply and how to place an order.
    Request a birth certificate

  • Request a marriage certificate

    See where to go depending on when the marriage took place. Book an appointment to request in person, or order online.
    Request a marriage certificate

  • Register a domestic partnership

    Learn who can qualify to become "registered domestic partners." Read how to register, what the benefits are, and how to end the partnership.
    Register a domestic partnership

Professional licenses and permits

  • Educator licensure

    Find the forms and information to apply for or renew your license in education.
    See educator license resources

  • Medical and health field licenses

    View the list of licensing boards in the Maryland Department of Health. Select the board for your field to learn about required training and licenses.
    Find your medical or health field

  • Labor licenses

    Follow the steps you need to take to get or renew your professional license for a broad range of fields.
    See the requirements for labor licenses and apply

Recreational permits

  • Fishing and crabbing licenses

    See a clear summary of state fishing and crabbing laws. Find the right registration for your type of activity.
    View all sport fishing and crabbing licenses

  • Hunting licenses and permits

    Access the guide to hunting and trapping in the state. Learn about the Apprentice Hunter Program, see new rules for crossbows, and more.
    Look for hunting and trapping resources

Childcare & pre-K

  • Child care scholarship program

    The Child Care Scholarship Program helps families pay for child care and early education.
    See if you're eligible for child care support

  • Maryland pre-K programs

    Find high quality pre-K for children who are 3 and 4 years old. Maryland works with public schools and private centers to give you more choices.
    Choose a pre-K program near you

  • Mental health support for infants and children

    Consultants work with families, programs, and teachers. Their job is to find and treat mental health problems in children.
    Read about available support services

K-12 education

  • Local school systems

    View contact information for all 24 public school systems in the state.
    Find your local school system

  • Special education services

    Learn about special education programs for children 0 - 21. Get access to resources for families, educators, and providers.
    Explore all special ed programs and support

  • Home schooling

    Get the facts about home instruction and connect with support.
    View home schooling options

  • Student support services

    Connect with resources that support the success of all students. These programs are available for parents, students, and educators.
    See available student support services

Continuing and higher education

  • College prep

    See the different pathways to earn college prep diplomas. Explore resources to get students set up for success in college.
    Start your college prep journey

  • Choosing a college

    Browse resources to help you choose and pay for college.
    Get help choosing a college

  • University System of Maryland (USM)

    Access an affordable education to start or grow your career.
    Learn more about USM

  • Community colleges

    Start your future today at one of 16 community colleges. Get an affordable education for a transfer degree, job training, or lifelong learning.
    Find a community college near you

  • Scholarships and financial aid

    View an updated list of state grants and scholarships that can help pay for your education.
    See if you qualify for financial aid

  • Save for education expenses

    The state offers an investment plan to help you save for education. You can use the savings for many school-related expenses, and anyone can contribute.
    Sign up for a Maryland 529 account

    Whether you're ready to start, or looking to grow your child care career, find the info you need. Get training and licensing help as well as business and marketing tips.

  • Childcare provider portal

    Child care providers can use this portal to renew a license, track attendance, and more.
    Explore the childcare provider portal

  • Become a Maryland teacher

    Discover what it takes to become a teacher, and all the rewards that follow. If you are a student planning for college or an adult seeking a new career, there's a path for you.
    Explore a teaching career

  • Apply for or renew your certification

    Find the forms and information to apply for or renew your certification in education.
    Browse educator certification resources

  • Education grant programs

    Read about grant programs for educators. See which grants are currently open for applications.
    View all education grant programs

  • Professional learning programs

    Discover new ways to grow as an educator. See courses and events to improve your skills and boost student success.
    Explore professional learning programs

Environment actions

  • Climate change

    The Climate Change Program is working to improve our world. We can reduce our impact through policies and analysis.
    Check out the Climate Change Program

  • Air quality monitoring

    This program tracks and reports air quality levels. It also works with universities to help make our air cleaner.
    See current air quality conditions

  • Air quality forecast

    Get 3-day air quality forecasts across ten regions. Learn what steps to take to reduce your exposure to poor air quality.
    Find the air quality forecast for your region

  • Water quality resources

    Check out information about keeping our water clean and safe. View recent maps, data, and advisories about water quality.
    Learn more about Maryland’s water quality

  • Electronics recycling

    Discover how to recycle your old electronics. This reduces waste and keeps toxins out of landfills.
    Locate an e-recycling collection site near you

  • Current weather conditions

    The Maryland Mesonet provides a variety of weather data, updated every minute to help you stay prepared and safe.

Maryland supports healthy starts and good nutrition for all ages.

  • Find out if you qualify for SNAP, WIC, and SUN Bucks and apply today

Check eligibility for food and nutrition benefits

  • See if you qualify

    Use our five-minute screener to find out what benefits you can get.
    Find out if you are eligible for food and nutrition benefits

  • Food assistance for women and young children

    If you are pregnant, a new mother, or have a child under five, Women, Infants, and Children (WIC) can help. This program offers nutrition advice, breastfeeding support, and healthy foods.
    Learn about WIC and make an appointment today

  • Food assistance for low-income households

    The Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) helps low-income households buy healthy food.
    Find out how to apply for SNAP

  • Farmers market money for older adults

    Eligible older adults can receive money to buy fresh fruits and vegetables. The money can be used at local farmers markets and farm stands.
    Apply to get your farmers market subsidy

  • SUN Bucks

    Eligible students (ages 5-18) can get money for food during the summer when school is out.
    Read more and get enrolled in SUN Bucks

  • Community meals for older adults

    There are more than 250 places in Maryland where older adults can get a meal. These spots are great for meeting people, learning about nutrition, and taking part in health programs.
    Find a community meal near you

  • Home delivered meals for older adults

    If you're an older adult with mobility issues, you might be eligible to get nutritious meals brought to you.
    Connect to a meal delivery service in your area
